TNECD's Nov. 16, 2026 release confirms Copperweld will invest $56 million in a new advanced manufacturing facility of about 250,000 sq ft on Copperweld Drive and create 40 jobs across multiple Fayetteville locations. It also confirms the company is headquartered in Fayetteville and that its 2021 and 2022 expansions created more than 200 jobs in Lincoln County.

item: Toledo Molding & Die (First Brands Group) WARN
findings: TDLWD WARN letter dated March 4, 2026 (WARN #202500038): First Brands Group, LLC, permanent closure effective April 30, 2026, at TMD Fayetteville, 11 East Park Dr., affecting 333 Tennessee employees. All dashboard figures match; the letter says 'TMD' and does not spell out Toledo Molding & Die.
TDLWD WARN letter dated Jan. 13, 2026 (WARN #202500027): permanent closure effective July 31, 2026, 80 affected workers, 100 Northcreek Drive, Shelbyville. All dashboard figures match.

TDLWD WARN letter dated Oct. 30, 2025 (WARN #202500017): temporary layoff effective Jan. 5, 2026, 710 Tennessee employees at 301 Donald F. Ephlin Pkwy, Spring Hill; the letter's distribution list includes the Maury County mayor. The note's statement that GM expected the pause to last until about mid-2026 is not in the letter; I could only find it in news reports (Tier 2), and I did not check whether production has since restarted.
suggested_fix: Attribute the mid-2026 restart expectation to news reports (or link GM's own statement), and update the note if production has resumed.

findings: TDLWD WARN letter dated Oct. 7, 2025 (WARN #202500009): permanent layoff effective Nov. 21, 2025, 82 affected workers at 763 Beechcroft Rd, Spring Hill. The letter is addressed to the Spring Hill and Maury County mayors, which supports the Maury County label. All dashboard figures match.
suggested_fix: Optional: replace 'news reports described a permanent layoff' with 'the state WARN letter describes a permanent layoff'.

item: Manchester Coffee County Conference Center WARN
findings: TDLWD WARN letter dated June 11, 2025 (WARN #202400076): the Public Building Authority for the City of Manchester, doing business as the Manchester Coffee County Conference Center, filed for a permanent layoff effective July 1, 2025, affecting 27 workers at 147 Hospitality Blvd., Manchester. TDLWD WARN letter dated April 22, 2025 (WARN #202400068): permanent closure effective June 27, 2025, 95 affected workers at 2206 Oakland Parkway, Columbia. All dashboard figures match.

I opened the TDLWD WARN letter this week. It is dated April 16, 2025 (WARN #202400065) and reports a 'permanent closure' effective June 13, 2025, affecting 47 workers at 1 Cedar King Road, Shelbyville. The dashboard's date, worker count and city are right, but it lists the action as 'Layoff', and its note says the letter could not be opened and concludes it 'was not a full closure'. The official letter contradicts both. A separate Corsicana Bedding site may still operate in Shelbyville, but the notice itself is for a closure.
suggested_fix: Change the action to 'Closure' and replace the note with: 'State WARN letter: permanent closure effective June 13, 2025, at 1 Cedar King Road, Shelbyville, affecting 47 workers.'

findings: TDLWD WARN letter dated Feb. 5, 2025 (WARN #202400054): permanent layoff beginning April 1, 2025, with all separations expected to be complete by July 31, 2025. It affects 162 workers at 2004 Remke Ave., Lawrenceburg. All dashboard figures match.
suggested_fix: Optional: add that this was a permanent layoff with separations running through July 31, 2025.

findings: TVA's own Aug. 20, 2026 board press release (seen only as a search result; the PDF host is blocked from this session) confirms the Board changed its wholesale rate structure to address data center load growth. findings: TNECD's Sept. 24, 2026 release confirms Chester, Cumberland and Putnam counties were selected for PEP, and that letters of intent for the next round are due by Jan. 14, 2027.

TDLWD's Oct. 15, 2026 release confirms the new TNTalent program is part of the TNWorks Talent Accelerator. It says Tennessee-based employers can tap $5 million in federal funding for workforce development in nuclear energy, AI infrastructure and advanced manufacturing, and it points employers to TNWorks.com.

TNECD's Oct. 28, 2026 release lists 14 recipients: Centerville (Hickman) $300,000, Collinwood (Wayne) $125,000 and Mount Pleasant (Maury) $325,000, which total $750,000 for the region. The 14 listed awards add up to exactly $3,900,568 (the release says 'more than $3.9 million'). The release also confirms a 25% match for new recipients.

TNECD's Oct. 27, 2026 release names 14 counties: Carter, Clay, Cocke, Cumberland, Dickson, Greene, Marshall, Overton, Putnam, Sequatchie, Scott, Sullivan, Sumner and Unicoi. Marshall is the only one of the 13 SMTN counties. It confirms Points Consulting will do a site visit and a customized housing review, and it states no dollar amount or timeline.

USDA's ARC program page and its Federal Register notice (seen as official search results; rd.usda.gov is blocked from this session) say letters of interest are accepted from 11:59 a.m. ET Oct. 19, 2026 until 11:59 a.m. ET Nov. 20, 2026. They say the grant portion may reach 25% of total award costs but not more than $20 million, and that the program is for rural electric cooperatives' nuclear energy and transmission efficiency projects. USDA's newsroom release gives the same dates and a $175 million program size.
TNECD's ARC application page states that planning grants are accepted quarterly with a $100,000 limit, on Nov. 13, 2026, Feb. 12, 2027 and June 11, 2027. All dashboard details match.

TBR's June 25, 2026 release (seen as a tbr.edu search result; the site is blocked from this session) says the College System will launch a new 600-hour Tile Manufacturing Operator program in fall 2026 at TCAT Dickson, TCAT Hohenwald and TCAT Upper Cumberland. TBR's ceramic tile sector page lists 'TCAT Hohenwald (main campus & Maury County Instructional Service Center)'. TCAT Hohenwald's homepage lists the program.

item: Acumen picks Sumner County for first U.S. plant
findings: TNECD's Nov. 12, 2026 release confirms Taiwan-based toothbrush and oral care maker Acumen will invest $20.2 million in a 90,000 sq ft plant in Sumner County (Gallatin), with 50 jobs initially and plans for hundreds more. item: Fed held rates Oct 28; two dissents favored a hike
findings: The Federal Reserve's Oct. 28, 2026 statement (seen as a federalreserve.gov search result; the site is blocked from this session) shows the range held at 3-3/4 to 4 percent on a 10-2 vote. 'Voting against the monetary policy action were Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack', who preferred a 1/4-point increase. News reports identify Hammack as Cleveland Fed President, not a governor, so 'two governors' is inaccurate. I did not verify the '10-Yr Treasury near 5%' context.
suggested_fix: Change 'two governors' to 'Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack' (or 'two members').
